issue_context.title: Inconsistent Label Matchers in Remote Read Requests
comments: Let me provide some additional context regarding this issue. The primary concern with this problem is that it causes alerting rules to evaluate incorrect values, resulting in false alerts being triggered. Although the occurrence rate is very low, it seems that no expected alerts are being missed. However, alerts that should not be triggered are being incorrectly sent.

I believe that I've got the same issue with RemoteRead. Some matchers are missing, some keys are duplicated.
We've encountered that problem right after the update from 2.37.6 to 2.53.1.

FWIW, I've heard that recently Prometheus got some internal string pool to reduce memory footprint.
The whole issue seems like a memory corruption thing for me.

After updating Prometheus from version 2.47.1 to 2.53.2 in our environment, we have observed an increase in false alerts. We noticed that the order of the label matchers was changing in version 2.47.1 as well, so it's possible that this issue existed before the update. However, the frequency of occurrence seems to have increased since the update.

Thanks for the report,
This indeed looks like a data race.
I assume the Prometheus instance can also serve such queries, so somewhere we try to run both the requests concurrently using the same `matchers` but somewhere we alter `matchers`.
I'll look into this.

By running one Prometheus instance, with the data race detector enabled, on 9090, with:

```
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: prom1
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["localhost:9090"]

remote_read:
  - url: http://doesntmatther:9999/read
    read_recent: true
    required_matchers:
      job: prom1
```

Then run `curl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=up{job="prom1",foo=~"bar", bar!~"foo"}'`

The easiest/safest solution would be to pass copies of `matchers` here https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/3a82cd5a7ed4c5e9b530fafcb779c2e9c81e2aab/storage/merge.go#L154-L162

to not be prone to changes like in:

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/3a82cd5a7ed4c5e9b530fafcb779c2e9c81e2aab/tsdb/querier.go#L237-L243

I'll try to reproduce this in a test and I'll propose a fix.

review_comments: needed as the race detector is disabled on tests currently.
Kind of sad to re-alloc here. Can we make sure for the moment we are about to modify those, only then we re-alloc?

Yep, I left a comment about that here https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/14983#discussion_r1775736242, I'm concerned that approach isn't future proof (no guarantee that we'll not alter that slice somewhere else), however, if you believe it’s worth the risk, we can copy the slice before sorting n `blockQuerier`.

copying is ~8bytes per matcher (+some constant bytes), given the common use cases I'm aware of (there are no benchmarks that emphasize 10,000 matchers use cases e.g.) for the read API, I think that overhead could be negligible; for prometheus, supposing `queriers#=2`, `queryConcurrency=20`, `avg_select_duration=100ms` and 5 matchers per query, we'll be producing ~`2*20*5*8=1600bytes` of garbage every `100ms` = ~`16kB/s` in the worst case.

We could also consider pooling for this, but avoiding additional complexity would be preferable.
cc @bwplotka in case this went unnoticed.
I don't think that preventing blockQuerier from altering the matchers or assuming no other querier will respect that in the future is a good/safe solution.
for better readability? AFAIK, `copy()` is generally faster than `append()` (which is used by `slices.Clone()`)
